summary: Establishes the four-post experienced digital product core across the three-year mobilisation, sustained agentic-development capability and a supervised junior-engineering placement in Years Two and Three to deliver King’s Edge and the Digital Student Experience Hub and build an enduring product-development capability.
detailSummary:
Digital Innovation and Product Development Capability establishes the team and working practices through which King’s Edge and the Digital Student Experience Hub are delivered. The current planning assumption is that the same four-post experienced core is required throughout the three-year mobilisation to June 2029. From Year Two, that core is deliberately augmented by one paid sandwich-year Junior Full-Stack Engineer per year as a supervised capability and talent-pipeline test. Evidence still determines whether further capacity is needed and which elements should continue beyond mobilisation.

The experienced core is 4.0 FTE across four explicit posts. The planning profile is: Senior Backend & Integration Engineer, £61,000 in 2026/27 and £91,000 in each full year thereafter; Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer, £50,000 then £75,000 per full year; Product & Service Designer, £50,000 then £75,000 per full year; and QA Engineer, £42,000 then £63,000 per full year. Together the experienced core profiles at approximately £203,000 in 2026/27, £304,000 in 2027/28 and £304,000 in 2028/29, or approximately £811,000 across mobilisation in constant 2026 planning prices. Digital and IT / HR must validate final grades, appointment points, start dates and future pay awards.

In 2027/28 and again in 2028/29, the team adds one 1.0 FTE Junior Full-Stack Engineer through a paid sandwich-year placement. A £35,000 annual employment envelope is used for planning in each year, giving £70,000 across the two placement cycles. The placement student works on a supervised, bounded and lower-risk backlog and is explicitly additional to the four experienced posts. The purpose is both productive delivery and institutional learning: to test useful junior contribution, supervision cost, learning value, use of agentic tooling and the potential for a repeatable student-to-digital-talent pipeline. Total planned staffing is therefore approximately £203,000 in Year One and £339,000 in each of Years Two and Three, or approximately £881,000 across mobilisation.

Mark Peace is the Product Owner during mobilisation. The funded team is supported by approximately 0.2 FTE Business Analysis during the main discovery period, approximately 0.2 FTE DevOps/platform support, and up to approximately 0.2 FTE solution architecture only if the Senior Backend & Integration Engineer cannot credibly carry that function. Specialist assurance is drawn from existing institutional functions when required.

Ring-fenced agentic software-development tooling is treated as part of the engineering model throughout all three mobilisation years, currently profiled at £90,000 per year or £270,000 in total. The amount remains subject to commercial validation, including whether existing shared capacity can reduce actual spend. The directly quantified 4.1.3 profile is approximately £293,000 in Year One and £429,000 in each of Years Two and Three, or approximately £1.151m across the three-year mobilisation before valuing existing shared capacity.

caseForChange.problem: King’s does not currently have a sufficiently dependable multidisciplinary product capability for turning emerging student-experience needs into working, supported digital services at pace. King’s needs sustained in-house capability to deliver the King’s Edge roadmap, establish and evolve the Digital Student Experience Hub, and support broader discovery and integration across the student digital estate.
caseForChange.opportunity: A four-post experienced product core across the three-year mobilisation, combined with lean shared Business Analysis, DevOps/platform and conditional solution-architecture support, gives King’s a disciplined route from need to supported change. Sustained agentic software-development tooling allows agentic delivery to become part of normal engineering practice rather than a short pilot. Once the experienced team and practices are established, a supervised sandwich-year Junior Full-Stack Engineer in Years Two and Three creates a low-risk way to test additional delivery capacity and a potential internal digital-talent pipeline.
caseForChange.whyNow: King’s Edge is moving into rapid replatforming and substantial product development, while the Digital Student Experience Hub needs a focused September 2027 first release and then sustained development across the remainder of mobilisation. 2026/27 is the right point to recruit the experienced core and establish the tooling and shared capacity; from 2027/28 the team should be mature enough to host a sandwich-year engineer safely and productively.
caseForChange.intendedChange: Across the three-year mobilisation, the funded 4.0 FTE experienced core delivers the King’s Edge roadmap and the Digital Student Experience Hub, supported by sustained agentic tooling. In Years Two and Three, one paid sandwich-year Junior Full-Stack Engineer per year augments the core on a supervised, bounded backlog and provides evidence about junior contribution, supervision, learning and future talent-pipeline potential. By June 2029, King’s should have enough evidence to decide which elements of the experienced core, agentic tooling and placement model should continue as recurrent business-as-usual capability.

benefits.title: King’s responds more quickly to emerging student needs
benefits.statement: Priority needs can be translated into tested digital responses in shorter cycles, with student and staff evidence shaping development before large commitments are made.
benefits.realisationPeriod: From establishment of the first delivery pipeline
benefits.successLooksLike: Priority needs move predictably from discovery to evaluated live use, and users can influence solutions while they remain adaptable.

benefits.title: Digital delivery becomes more predictable and evidence-led
benefits.statement: A transparent pipeline, explicit capacity decisions and consistent product and assurance practices make needs, priorities, progress and trade-offs clearer.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, Digital and IT and King’s
benefits.realisationPeriod: As the operating model becomes routine
benefits.successLooksLike: Demand is prioritised through one route, delivery commitments are visible and changes in team capacity can be explained by actual roadmap evidence.

benefits.title: Successful innovation becomes sustainable institutional provision
benefits.statement: Valuable changes have a defined route into secure, supported and appropriately owned operation, while multidisciplinary capability remains available for continuous improvement.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, Digital and IT and King’s
benefits.successLooksLike: Successful capabilities have explicit ownership and support arrangements, unsuccessful trials close cleanly, and the product capability has an evidence-based route into business as usual.

steps.title: Recruit and mobilise the core multidisciplinary digital product team
steps.summary: From September through November 2026, secure three-year mobilisation funding and recruit or assign the four experienced core posts through Digital and IT. Confirm Mark Peace as Product Owner, lean shared Business Analysis and DevOps/platform capacity, conditional solution architecture, and the commercial route for the £90,000 annual agentic software-development tooling allowance across all three mobilisation years.

steps.title: Establish the product operating model and delivery practices
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish one transparent pipeline, prioritisation and capacity cadence, proportionate discovery and user involvement, engineering and quality expectations, sustained agentic-development practices, embedded assurance and release practices across King’s Edge and the Digital Student Experience Hub.

steps.title: Prove the capability through King’s Edge, broad discovery and the focused Hub release
steps.summary: From January to October 2027, prove that the four-post experienced core and lean shared-capacity model can deliver the substantive King’s Edge roadmap and focused Digital Student Experience Hub release. Use the evidence to refine the operating model and prepare a safe, supervised Year Two sandwich-year engineering placement.

steps.title: Make product operations and live-service collaboration routine
steps.summary: From November 2027 to February 2028, make operating practices routine across the live Digital Student Experience Hub and King’s Edge product domain and add one supervised sandwich-year Junior Full-Stack Engineer as additional Year Two delivery and learning capacity alongside the four-post experienced core.

steps.title: Scale the team and its practices where the wider roadmap justifies it
steps.summary: From March to October 2028, use live-service and first-placement evidence to refine the capability model, continue the planned sandwich-year Junior Full-Stack placement for a second year in 2028/29, and approve any further expansion only where roadmap demand and evidence justify it.

steps.title: Embed an enduring institutional product-development capability
steps.summary: By the end of the three-year mobilisation, establish the sustainable multidisciplinary capability, professional leadership, governance, product practices and interfaces with SED product ownership and Digital and IT specialist/platform services. Decide which elements of the four-post experienced core, agentic tooling and junior-placement model should continue after June 2029 and confirm recurrent staffing, tooling and costs from live evidence before business-as-usual transition.
